::: {.hero}
[Ecoinformatics Lab · Valdivia, Chile]{.eyebrow}

# Living systems leave traces. We read them.

::: {.lede}
We work where ecology, complex systems and urban science meet. We use mobile phone
records, censuses, satellite imagery and biodiversity data to understand how cities,
populations and the forests of southern Chile organise themselves.
:::

![](assets/hero-network.svg)
:::

::: {.content-block}

[Lines of work]{.eyebrow}

::: {.threads}
::: {.thread}
### Urban scaling
How a city's properties change with its size: productivity, occupational diversity,
water consumption, material footprint. Scaling laws brought to bear on urban policy.
:::

::: {.thread}
### Networks and segregation
Voice-call networks across cities in Chile and Brazil, read as a measure of
interactional segregation: who talks to whom, across the socioeconomic gradient.
:::

::: {.thread}
### Computational ecology
Species distributions, landscape fragmentation, wildfire and irrecoverable carbon in
protected areas. Quantitative methods for conserving the Valdivian temperate forest.
:::
:::

## The lab

The Ecoinformatics Lab has run since 2008 within the Instituto de Conservación,
Biodiversidad y Territorio at Universidad Austral de Chile. Undergraduate, master's
and doctoral students, scientific programmers and visiting researchers have passed
through it, and now work in universities, public agencies and industry in Chile and
abroad.

This site gathers that work: the projects, the publications and the people who made
them.

[Meet the team and the lab's alumni](people.qmd)

:::
